messages:
mira: Heads-up — saw a bunch of noisy ECC/Xid alerts last night on gpunode-12 and gpunode-17. Mostly short bursts (1-3s) but Alertmanager fired repeatedly.
ops-bot: ALERT GPU_ECC_SPIKE firing for instance=gpunode-12 gpu_index=0 severity=warning
alex: Any idea if this is transient (driver/kernel) or an actual card starting to fail? Do we have metrics to differentiate?
mira: DCGM exporter shows spikes in `ecc.correctable.count` and intermittent `xid` logs. Pattern looks bursty, not steady. I dug into `/var/log/nvidia/gpu-events.log` — lots of Xid 31 with very short intervals.
sam: Thinking out loud: rule probably too sensitive. We should prefer a windowed increase() over a simple rate or instant value. Also group alerts by instance (node) for triage, but keep per-card counts in the annotations.
jen: We do want to avoid masking a failing card by grouping too aggressively. Proposal: require 5+ correctable ECC events per gpu_index over a 15m window before alerting, and add a debounce for transient bursts.
alex: Agreed. Prototype rule:
```yaml
- alert: GPU_ECC_Persistent
  expr: sum by(instance, gpu_index) (increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[15m])) > 5
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Persistent ECC correctable spikes on {{ $labels.instance }} (gpu {{ $labels.gpu_index }})"
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-triage"
```
mira: I like that. The `for: 5m` plus `increase()` should filter short 1-2s bursts.
sam: Also add an alertmanager route that groups by `instance` so ops receives a single ticket per node with per-card details in the payload. We can keep `gpu_index` in the payload and in Grafana panel.
jen: For extremely noisy nodes (flapping), we should have a temporary auto-silence created by an automation if we detect >50 bursts in 1h — put them into a short maintenance state and schedule a hardware check.
alex: Can someone test this in staging? If it behaves, we can roll to prod tomorrow during the 03:00 UTC maintenance window.
mira: I'll push the rule to staging and run a synthetic spike generator against the DCGM metrics to validate. I'll also link the triage runbook and escalation matrix here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-triage
ops-bot: Silence created for alert GPU_ECC_SPIKE on gpunode-17 for 30m by mira
sam: One more small ask — add `card_vendor` and `sku` as labels/annotations so hardware team can prioritize replacements without digging logs.
jen: Good point. Also include last_seen timestamp and the aggregated count in the annotation.
mira: Plan: staging test tonight, if green roll to prod 03:00 UTC with rule: 15m window, threshold 5, 5m `for`, alertmanager grouping by `instance`, and auto-silence for very high-frequency flappers. I'll post results here after the run.
alex: SGTM :thumbsup:
